claims: A functional frontier profile rules out simultaneous global no-worse dominance.
Raw functional frontier semantics inherit the functional no-simultaneous-dominance theorem once admissible raw objects supply the required extracted profile.
Original-HODL first-even expansion payloads rule out simultaneous global no-worse in slippage and original-HODL curvature.
Original-HODL witness-family semantics lift pairwise expansion obligations into a no-admissible-simultaneous-dominance theorem.
The CPMM budget route proves same-price no-free-lunch under explicit pathwise slippage, bounded-state, and price-path hypotheses.
Raw symmetric homogeneous AMM wrappers can reuse the CPMM budget theorem when their normalized defect field satisfies the declared derivative and path hypotheses.
Unconstrained coefficient surfaces and weak raw coefficient extractors admit simultaneous dominance countermodels, proving the extraction obligations are load-bearing.
proof_method: abstract functional frontier antitone operator proofs
CPMM collapsed-budget derivative and pathwise integration lemmas
countermodel construction for missing semantic assumptions

boundaries: This is a conditional theorem layer. It does not prove that every concrete AMM implementation satisfies the raw semantic extraction obligations.
The CPMM budget theorem requires explicit pathwise slippage and price-path hypotheses.
The raw wrappers require positivity, homogeneity, symmetry, differentiability, bounded defect fields, and derivative/path assumptions where stated.
The countermodel theorems are negative knowledge: they show why unconstrained coefficient surfaces and weak raw extractors are insufficient.
This proof package is real-analysis theorem work and does not replace integer-runtime or bytecode-level AMM verification.
